thread:
Samir: Quick follow-up from the outage postmortem — we need to lock down customer-facing language and the action-item tracker before we publish anything to the status page or send customer summaries.

Ava: +1. Do we have a single canonical status-page blurb to iterate on?

Samir: Draft below. Please suggest edits. We want something non-technical but transparent, and we need legal/pss review before pushing.

Samir: DRAFT STATUS BLURB:
We experienced degraded API availability for the Redwood hosted inference service between 02:14 and 02:42 UTC. The root cause was an autoscaling misconfiguration that exhausted GPU allocation for a small set of models. Normal service was restored after an emergency capacity increase and configuration rollback. We’re implementing configuration validation and improved alerting to prevent recurrence.

Marcus: I like the clarity. Suggest adding: "No customer data was exposed" if Priya confirms.

Priya: Confirming — no data exposure. We should add a short line about when the full RCA will be available and how customers can request a copy.

Leah: How about: "A detailed post-incident report (RCA) will be published to our status page and shared with affected customers within 5 business days."

Jon: We should also call out the mitigation/fallbacks we used in plain terms: increased capacity and rollback of the recent autoscale policy change. Keeps trust high.

Samir: Updated draft with Leah/Jon edits below. Anyone object to publishing this after Priya sign-off?

Samir: UPDATED DRAFT:
We experienced degraded API availability for the Redwood hosted inference service between 02:14 and 02:42 UTC. The issue was caused by a recent autoscaling configuration change that exhausted reserved GPU capacity for a small set of models. Service was restored after a controlled capacity increase and rollback of the misconfiguration. No customer data was exposed. A detailed post-incident report (RCA) will be published to our status page and shared with affected customers within 5 business days.

Ava: Looks good. I can paste this into the status page once Priya clears legal wording.

Priya: Cleared. Minor suggestion: replace "detailed" with "final" so it doesn't imply ongoing edits.

Samir: Good call. Finalizing language now.

Marcus: On the customer summaries: do we want a short, slightly more technical note for direct email to enterprise customers?

Leah: Yes — include timeline, impact per region/tenant, and the mitigation steps. Keep it ~4 bullet points. Marcus, can you draft?

Marcus: Will do. Targeting a 1-paragraph + 4 bullets. ETA EOD today.

Samir: OK next: action-item tracker. From the postmortem we had 6 follow-ups. I'm listing owners and due dates — please confirm or propose new owners: 
• ACTION-1: Add autoscale config schema validation to CI — Owner: Jon — Due: 2026-03-30
• ACTION-2: Improve capacity forecasting for model spikes (weekly trend job) — Owner: Leah — Due: 2026-04-07
• ACTION-3: Status page template update for RCAs and timelines — Owner: Ava — Due: 2026-03-26
• ACTION-4: Create customer-facing RCA template + legal checklist — Owner: Priya — Due: 2026-03-29
• ACTION-5: Post-incident runbook for emergency capacity increases — Owner: Samir — Due: 2026-03-28
• ACTION-6: Trend analysis to detect recurring autoscale failures across last 6 months — Owner: Marcus & Eng-ML (ask eng-ml for a short report) — Due: 2026-04-14

Jon: Confirmed for ACTION-1. Will open PR and link here.

Leah: Confirmed for ACTION-2, will coordinate with forecasting infra.

Ava: Confirmed ACTION-3, will also add a checkbox for "legal review required" to the template.

Priya: Confirmed ACTION-4, will draft checklist and share sample language.

Samir: ACTION-5 noted. I'll create doc and schedule a tabletop this week for runbook validation.

Marcus: For ACTION-6 I'll ping eng-ml. Might need access to historical allocation logs — @jon can you grant?

Jon: Sure, will add Marcus to the analytics bucket and grant read-only.

Samir: One more thing — recurring incident pattern callout from the postmortem: autoscale policy changes + low-canary traffic produced unexpected config combos. We should treat this as a systemic risk. Any objections to adding a "recurring pattern" tag to the postmortem and creating a follow-up epic to address policy-change safeguards?

Leah: No objections. We should track that epic in product with measurable goals (reduce config-related outages by 80% in 6 months).

Marcus: Agree — epic would help prioritize. Also recommend weekly dashboard for autoscale policy change audits.

Priya: From a comms/privacy standpoint, we should ensure RCAs don't include sensitive logs. Use redacted attachments for customer-facing copies.

Samir: Good call. ACTION-7: Produce redacted customer RCA workflow (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-29) — adding to tracker.

incident-bot: A follow-up checklist has been created: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-113/followups (automated)

Samir: Thanks all. I'll push the status-page update after Priya signs off and once Ava confirms the template is ready. We'll treat the action items above as the single source of truth; please update the internal tracker when you make progress.

Ava: I'll post the final blurb to #status-updates and ping @support for customer outreach once Marcus shares the enterprise note. :thumbsup:

Marcus: Enterprise note draft posted in this thread at 17:30 UTC — PTAL when you can.

Leah: Thanks team — closing this thread, keeping the tracker open for updates.
